items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 24:1
items.html: The part of the head covered with hairs is called the Galgalta, and it is the aspect of the MEM of Tzelem, in which the Yud does not go out of the air. And the part of the head without hairs, namely from the forehead and below, is called the face of the head, and it is the aspect of the LAMED of Tzelem, in which the Yud goes out of the air and light remains. And the face itself is also divided according to the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK, for each of the three aspects of Tzelem is included in the other, as in the words of the Rav above (Page 312, Item 39). The two ears and the forehead are the aspect of its MEM; the two eyes are the aspect of its LAMED; and the two cheeks, the nose with the two lips, the tongue, and the mouth are the aspect of its TZADIK. See Answer 23 above. (Part 1, Page 339, Item 96).
